card.statement: Share FlashMLA decode plans across compatible KV-cache groups within one metadata-building pass, conditional on the pinned H200 runner still creating duplicate plans. The supplied patch implements per-pass holder sharing; the author reports fewer planner launches on H20 TP8, using synthetic acceptance for serving measurements. That establishes an implementation mechanism, not an H200 benefit. Unlike small-head kernels, this change does not require TP4 or TP8 and can plausibly apply to TP1. Its value depends on exposed redundant planner work under real DSpark rejection. Reuse must preserve equal live lengths, masks and replay state, rather than merely matching tensor shapes. First inspect baseline membership and builder dispatch; then compare unchanged execution with sharing alone, preserving all serving settings and measuring primary-workload latency and throughput.
card.observed_bottleneck: No H200 bottleneck is measured. Supplied installed code shows same-type plan reuse but does not establish whether cross-group sharing already exists. The #58818 author reports 21 versus four planner launches per step on eight H20 GPUs at TP8/EP8; those counts cannot be assumed for TP1/DP4. H200 exposed planner time and effect size are unknown.
card.mechanism: Implementation evidence: #58818 creates a dictionary local to build_attn_metadata and shares holders keyed by block size, causality and decode SWA width. Transfer inference: eliminating repeated compatible planner launches can shorten decode's critical path without changing attention arithmetic. The improvement disappears if planning is already shared, groups are incompatible, or removed work is not exposed.
card.proposed_change: First inspect the pinned runner and all three affected files for equivalent sharing and actual builder use. If absent and eligible, port the per-pass dictionary and holder reuse. Preserve separate target, drafter and microbatch passes; retain per-group behavior when compatibility cannot be established.

card.applicability: Plausible SM90 transfer independent of small local attention-head counts. Qualification is deferred pending baseline membership, active runner, compatible group composition and graph-replay correctness. V1 callers without the dictionary and separately built drafter metadata do not automatically benefit. The source performance setup differs in topology, model revision, prefix caching, Engram placement and speculative acceptance.
card.predicted_direction: Conditionally lower decode TPOT and improve output throughput; little direct prefill benefit is expected. Magnitude, TTFT-tail effects and saturation benefit are unknown.

alternatives.explanation: The baseline already shares plans, or only one compatible group executes.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: Inspect holder identity and lifetime, then count planner launches per eligible metadata pass and layer type. Already-shared execution has no incremental delta.

Preserve native agent-f75 8K/1K prefixes and fixed-schedule Mooncake anchors adapted to seq64. Keep 1K/1K diagnostics separate.
experiment.metrics: Activation: shared-holder uses divided by compatible group/layer-type opportunities, plus planner launches per eligible pass, separately for target/drafter and eager/graph execution on every rank. Serving: request TPOT=(last-first token time)/(server output tokens-1), excluding undefined one-token cases; TTFT tails, exact output tokens, throughput, historical-scorer goodput and replay lag. Record all-rank draft/verify/accepted deltas, KV blocks, preemption, missing coverage and resets. Measure exposed planner time only in separate diagnostics.

card.statement: Test direct paged candidate-only indexer scoring as a conditional replacement for dense scoring followed by masking in consumer layers. The supplied #62463 patch describes reading candidate K in place and retaining device-resident live lengths; #62000 instead gathers K before scoring. These are competing implementations of the same work-elimination mechanism, not cumulative optimizations. H20 evidence is conflicting: gathering regressed at one request, while direct scoring's lower ITL came from tiny samples and did not consistently improve throughput. The transfer hypothesis is that avoiding both discarded scoring and intermediate K copies helps eligible H200 long-context decode. First establish actual indexer shapes, cache format and baseline dispatch. Keep dense scoring as the short-context comparator and default; require native 8K/1K evidence before claiming a useful change to this deployment.
card.observed_bottleneck: No H200 scoring bottleneck is measured. #62000 reports profiler-derived improvements at approximately 1M context and nine requests on H20 TP8, but an approximately 11.6% single-request regression. #62463 reports lower mean ITL on H20 TP8 with 1,029,974 input and 16,384 output tokens, using only one run per arm and 2/4/8/16 requests at C1/2/4/8. At C4, overall completion throughput fell 1.5%. Its profiling batches also differed. These are author-reported results, not independently verified H200 observations.
card.mechanism: Implementation evidence: #62463 exposes direct paged candidate scoring with compact logits and device-side causal-bound preparation; #62000 exposes candidate-K gathering and default-off controls. Both avoid full compressed-context scoring for consumers. Transfer inference: direct reads may additionally avoid gather workspace traffic and fixed copy cost. Benefits depend on actual indexer shapes and context-to-candidate width, not TP-local attention-head padding.
card.proposed_change: First inspect complete installed call sites, patch integration, FP8 indexer-cache layout, context-parallel configuration and actual consumer dispatch. If eligible and absent, adapt #62463 to the pinned branch while preserving live device inputs and configuration-based graph selection. Keep dense scoring available. Evaluate #62000 as a separate mutually exclusive comparator; do not stack the implementations or infer a profitable H200 threshold from its example settings.

Alternative arm: candidate_gather.py and its supplied integration paths. The supplied patch excerpts do not include complete scoring and dispatch bodies.

Confirm actual indexer heads, strides, candidate widths, causal metadata and architecture gates. TP1's 64 attention heads neither prove nor disprove indexer-kernel compatibility. Candidate-source layers, pre-candidate layers and prefill remain outside the proposed change. Model accuracy, short-workload safety and H200 effect size are unknown.
card.predicted_direction: Potentially lower consumer-indexer time and long-context TPOT, especially when dense scoring scans substantially more positions than the candidate set. Short-context or low-row regressions remain plausible. No capacity, general throughput or primary-workload improvement is established.

card.statement: Port or activate DeepSelect for eligible FP32 indexer top-k calls on SM90, only after checking the installed selector and extension build. The supplied vLLM patch adds a Hopper availability path and explicit dtype, width, k and alignment checks. Its value would come from faster selection over unchanged logits, independently of attention-head padding or candidate scoring. However, the DeepSelect library's headline H20 results concern small-batch BF16 inputs, while this integration requires FP32; a commenter also reports a competing radix advantage at k=2048. Therefore, compare against the fastest eligible existing vLLM backend chosen on calibration workloads, not merely torch.topk. Preserve existing fallbacks and isolate this selector change initially with dense scoring. Any later compact-logit combination needs separate confirmation because the remaining selection workload is different.
card.observed_bottleneck: No H200 top-k bottleneck is measured. The supplied installed sparse-scoring helper explicitly gates DeepSelect to capability family 100, but the installed selector resolver is absent from the excerpts. #59204 supplies integration code without performance results. DeepSelect #14 reports H20 BF16 microbenchmarks; FP32 serving gains are unknown. Its competing-radix commenter supplies different k/length regimes, with hardware, dtype and timing units unknown.
card.mechanism: Implementation evidence: #59204 adds SM90 availability and Hopper FP32 validation, plus input/output alignment checks and bounded-row selection support. Transfer inference: a faster selector can reduce time spent selecting the same top-k from unchanged scores. This does not create an SM90 sparse-scoring kernel. The library's BF16 cluster-performance claim does not establish the behavior or speed of this FP32 integration.
card.proposed_change: First inspect the installed indexer_topk resolver, actual selected backend, extension revision and SM90 build targets. If a useful delta exists, port the compatible #59204 selector integration and explicitly select DeepSelect only for validated inputs, retaining the best native fallback. Do not broaden sparse_mqa_logits.has_deep_select indiscriminately because its downstream sparse-scoring dependencies are separate.
card.code_surface: vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py; vllm/config/kernel.py; cmake/external_projects/deepselect.cmake; relevant cache_utils integration and selector tests listed in #59204. Build and resolver changes are not fully visible in the supplied patch excerpt. The DeepSelect #14 kernel patch is unavailable in the supplied record.
card.applicability: Deferred pending rebase, compatible extension build, complete dispatch review and observed FP32 input contracts. Supplied checks require 0<k<=4096, width below 2^23, contiguous columns, a 128-byte-aligned input pointer and required input/output stride alignment. Actual k, width, row distribution and alignment are unknown. Compact candidate logits around 16K columns do not match #14's reported BF16 cluster regime starting at 128K.
card.predicted_direction: Potentially lower top-k latency and, if exposed, decode TPOT or cost per token. Gains may vanish or reverse for short rows, different k, larger row counts or already-competitive native kernels. H200 effect size is unknown.
